goal: Make the BlockToJsonVerbosity3 benchmark actually exercise prevout and fee lookups by giving it real undo data.
Fixes a benchmark that previously did the same work as a lower verbosity level, hiding the real cost.
reviewability: Ready to review, small self-contained change with a Tested ACK already verifying the numbers.
agreement: Strong support: ismaelsadeeq reproduced the benchmark and gave a Tested ACK (ismaelsadeeq).
Author raised a follow-up idea about block staleness but treated it as a non-blocking future improvement (0xB10C).

result.summary: This PR fixes the BlockToJsonVerbosity3 benchmark by adding real undo data (139KB) for block 413567 so that the benchmark actually exercises prevout and fee computation, which previously made it identical to Verbosity2. It updates CMakeLists.txt to embed the new data file and modifies rpc_blockchain.cpp to write the undo data into blockman storage before benchmarking. The author includes before/after benchmark numbers showing Verbosity3 now takes roughly double the time, reflecting the added undo-data-dependent work.
result.problem: The BlockToJsonVerbosity3 benchmark silently measured the same work as Verbosity2 because it lacked undo data, so developers benchmarking verbose block JSON output could not see the true cost of including prevouts and fees. This affects anyone optimizing or reviewing performance of blockToJSON for RPC callers like block explorers.

open_concerns: Author notes the 10-year-old test block may not give good benchmark coverage of the current per-script work (address encoding, descriptor inference) but explicitly frames this as a followup, not a blocker.

categories.rationale: Fixes a benchmark that was silently measuring the wrong thing (Verbosity3 was identical to Verbosity2 due to missing undo data), which is a real correctness issue in the benchmark's signal but has no runtime or security impact. Tested ACK confirms the fix works as intended and the numbers now differ meaningfully (29 op/s vs previous doubled time). Marginal in the priority chain since it only affects a rarely-used dev benchmark, not production code or CI gating.

uncertainties: No strong evidence this benchmark is actively used to drive optimization decisions, so its leverage on other work is speculative beyond the author's own comment.
result.card: This PR fixes the BlockToJsonVerbosity3 benchmark, which previously lacked undo data and therefore performed identical work to the lower Verbosity2 benchmark, hiding the true cost of including prevouts and fees in verbose block JSON. The author adds 139KB of real undo data for block 413567 and updates the benchmark setup to use it, showing before/after numbers where Verbosity3 now roughly doubles in time as expected. ismaelsadeeq reproduced the benchmark and gave a Tested ACK, confirming correctness. The author raised a non-blocking follow-up idea about using a more representative (recent) block for better benchmark coverage of modern script types, deferring it to a future PR. The change is small, self-contained, and ready to merge with no open concerns.
